section_1.title: The Intuitive Foundation: The 'Zeno's Rabbit' Approach
section_1.content: Introduce the concept of a limit by visualizing a rabbit jumping toward a carrot placed at x=2. The rabbit halves its distance with every jump. Even if it never technically 'reaches' the coordinate, we can define its 'target' position. Emphasize that a limit describes behavior near a point, not at the point itself.
section_1.example: A rabbit at x=1 jumps to 1.5, then 1.75, then 1.875. As the number of jumps n approaches infinity, the position approaches 2.

section_2.title: The Epsilon-Delta Rigor: Building the 'Safety Bubble'
section_2.content: Transition from intuition to the formal definition. Use a graphical representation: a 'target' range epsilon (ε) on the y-axis, and a corresponding 'input' range delta (δ) on the x-axis. Explain that for any tiny error margin (ε) we choose, we can find a tiny input window (δ) that keeps the function inside the target.
section_2.example: Visualizing a 'box' around the limit point (L); shrinking the height of the box (ε) forces the width (δ) to shrink to maintain function inclusion.

section_3.title: L'Hôpital's Rule: The Shortcut for Indeterminate Forms
section_3.content: Introduce the problem of 0/0 and ∞/∞ cases. Explain that when algebraic simplification (factoring) fails, we use the derivative of the numerator and denominator to find the slope ratio at the target point. Prerequisite: Students must understand that local linearity (derivatives) mirrors the behavior of functions near a point.
section_3.example: Calculating the limit of (sin x)/x as x -> 0. Visualizing the tangent lines of f(x)=sin x and g(x)=x at x=0; both share a slope, thus the limit is the ratio of their derivatives: cos(0)/1 = 1.

section_4.title: Synthesis & Summary
section_4.content: Review the progression: Limit (Where are we going?) -> Epsilon-Delta (How certain are we?) -> L'Hôpital (How do we compute it quickly?). Provide a high-level visual map connecting these concepts.
section_4.example: A 'Limit Toolbox' graphic: Intuition for 'Understanding,' Epsilon-Delta for 'Verification,' and L'Hôpital for 'Efficiency'.
